replies.author: @scott2862
replies.text:
Predatory rent hikes are when people rent from corporations of large scale companies with management, gyms, game rooms, pools, and hundreds of units per location. 

Renting the old school 2 and 3 bedroom apartments in cities of double and triple deckers are way cheaper than the lofty mills, smaller modern apartments with amenities you don’t need but cost big. 

Massachusetts here. 2 bedroom, living room, den, dining room, family size eat in kitchen, pantry, front porch and back porch laundry hookups and one car garage in a maintained and updated by code utility’s is $1,300 a month and I been here for 7 years with one rental increase. 3 I identical units in a middle class quiet family Neighborhood  of similar 1885 and 1930 Industrial Revolution built homes. 

A one bedroom, small kitchenette a descent living room in the lofty mills renovated by corporate developers in the same city is $3,300 and a parking spot rental a few streets away for $200 
With a contract guarantee to go up 10% annually is where people are making the rent mistake.  

Shopping for an apartment is never an internet searchable process. All insanity small big cost mega structures that were renovated from the ground up after siting abandoned and partially collapsed for 70 years isn’t a cheep endeavor but some how that’s where people think it’s normal rent across the city market. 

Word of mouth, Newspaper ads, shopping center community post borers  and trying to only view owner occupied or small business landlords with a few buildings are the best way to go. 

It’s not a fast or easy prospect and takes about a month working to see one a day before you find the right neighborhood, with an family vibe of mainly I call grandma era refreshed family city homes.

replies.text: A primary residence is a forced savings account with a roof, not a pure investment.
